text: Databases store and organize information so we can find it quickly. Most databases use tables, where rows hold records and columns hold fields. When you want to get data, you write queries, usually in SQL, a language designed for asking questions. Before building a database, you plan its structure, called data modeling, which decides how data connects. To speed up searches, you add indexes, like a book's index. Today, many systems use NoSQL databases instead of traditional SQL ones. SQL works well with fixed tables and clear relationships, while NoSQL handles flexible or fast-changing data.
